challenge.name: The Loyalty Data Audit
challenge.description: A legal audit flagged that loyalty basket data lacks valid consent records, breaking the legal basis for using it in forecasts. #requirements_reuben# demands the data contracts be fully automated and governed to enforce consent checks before any data enters the pipeline. #efficiency_emilia# argues that manual review is sufficient for now to avoid delaying the promotion planning cycle, though she might accept a middle ground if it does not stall the weekly leaflet.
challenge.roundIntroduction: The compliance team suspended access to the loyalty app basket feed after discovering that retention policies were not documented in the data contracts. The KPI definitions for the next promotion cycle were never formally agreed upon, leaving the team without a clear baseline for how to handle the missing personal data signals.

on_enter_ops.reason: compliance audit found missing consent fields in the schema

stalemate_ops.reason: legal team blocked KPI sign off due to unresolved data rights

roster.name: Efficiency Emilia
roster.role: Uses deep domain knowledge to define business goals, objectives, and KPIs. Aligns ML features with overarching product strategy and organizational roadmaps. Evaluates system performance, operational capability, and project costs.
roster.priorities: Applying deep domain knowledge to ensure models fulfill specific business goals. Aligning ML solutions with clear objectives, KPIs, and business goals. Making organization-level decisions and enhancing overall operational capability. Defining products by defining and optimizing product features.

roster.name: Requirements Reuben
roster.role: Architects secure and scalable production ML systems. Defines security requirements, ensures privacy compliance, and manages data governance. Conducts rigorous testing and validation to guarantee high product quality.
roster.priorities: Guaranteeing high product quality through rigorous testing of applications. Guaranteeing the integrity, confidentiality, and security of all ML assets. Meeting internal and external compliance and data protection standards. Keeping infrastructure stable, reproducible, and cost-controlled.

roster.name: Automation Alex
roster.role: Builds automated ML pipelines to ensure seamless integration and deployment. Prioritizes reliable infrastructure for frequent software deployments. Maintains system operational stability and focuses on CI/CD tooling.
roster.priorities: Building automated pipelines and maintaining full system operational stability. Ensuring seamless deployment, integration, and stability of models and services in production.

roster.name: Reliability Ruth
roster.role: Develops the end-user applications and services that integrate ML models. Handles model deployment, configuration, and continuous monitoring of real-world performance. Employs feedback loops to facilitate iterative improvements and system reliability.
roster.priorities: Pushes the delivery of reliable ML-powered features that directly improve the user experience. CI/CD and working feedback loops. Identifying and reporting issues to facilitate iterative improvements.

items.fact: {requirements_reuben} proposed moving the risk review hand-off, and the checks that follow it, off manual handling.

readings.driver: The less anyone has to push that chain by hand, the sooner audits clear without a scramble.
readings.boundary: He will not sign off on a release where that whole chain still needs manual pushing.
readings.trade_off: He would accept leaving one step of that chain manual if the rest moves on its own.
readings.fact: That is simply how the risk review chain runs today.

items.fact: {requirements_reuben} proposed that the consent rules be written into the data contracts before anything uses them.

readings.driver: A written contract would catch a missing consent field before it ever reaches a report.
readings.boundary: He will not accept loyalty data being used while the data contracts are missing or broken.
readings.trade_off: He would accept a lighter contract if it still covers consent fields specifically.
readings.fact: That is simply the state of the data contracts today, broken.

items.fact: {requirements_reuben} proposed leaving the KPI definitions exactly as hand reviewed as they are today.

readings.driver: Automating the KPI definitions would free up time for the data contracts audit instead.
readings.boundary: He will not accept the KPI definitions staying unreviewed through the next promotion cycle.
readings.trade_off: He would accept the KPI definitions staying hand reviewed if the data contracts audit lands first.
readings.fact: That is simply how the KPI definitions get checked today.

items.fact: {requirements_reuben} proposed trading part of his compliance budget for faster progress on the audit.

readings.driver: Spending more of that budget elsewhere would speed up work the team actually notices.
readings.boundary: He will not give up his entire compliance budget for one single audit.
readings.trade_off: He would give up part of his compliance budget if the audit moves forward.
readings.fact: That is simply how his compliance budget is split up this cycle.

items.fact: {efficiency_emilia} proposed a middle ground on how far the data contracts audit goes.

readings.driver: Pushing the audit all the way through would catch every gap before the next leaflet ships.
readings.boundary: She will not accept the audit stalling the weekly leaflet planning cycle entirely.
readings.trade_off: She would accept the audit staying partial if the leaflet planning cycle keeps moving.
readings.fact: That is simply how far the audit has gotten so far.

items.fact: {efficiency_emilia} proposed that the hand-off into ingestion carry a formal sign off.

readings.driver: A formal sign off there would catch a bad consent record before it reaches a report.
readings.boundary: She will not accept that hand-off shipping data without that formal sign off in place.
readings.trade_off: She would accept a lighter check there if the sign off still covers consent fields.
readings.fact: That is simply the current sign off status of that hand-off, nothing formal yet.

items.fact: {automation_alex} proposed moving risk assessment reviews off manual handling.

readings.driver: The less anyone has to review that by hand, the sooner releases clear without delay.
readings.boundary: He will not accept risk assessment staying hands on through the next release cycle.
readings.trade_off: He would accept risk assessment staying hands on a while longer if the audit lands first.
readings.fact: That is simply how risk assessment reviews are run today, by hand.

items.fact: {automation_alex} proposed shifting some of his automation budget toward the audit work instead.

readings.driver: Spending that budget elsewhere would speed up the pipeline changes the team is waiting on.
readings.boundary: He will not give up his entire automation budget for one single audit push.
readings.trade_off: He would give up part of his automation budget if the audit work moves forward.
readings.fact: That is simply how his automation budget is split up this cycle.

items.fact: {automation_alex} proposed leaving KPI governance exactly as relaxed as it is today.

readings.driver: A stricter KPI sign off would catch a bad metric before the next promotion cycle.
readings.boundary: He will not accept KPI definitions shipping with no review step at all forever.
readings.trade_off: He would accept KPI definitions keeping no formal review step if the audit lands first.
readings.fact: That is simply how little review the KPI definitions get right now.

items.fact: {reliability_ruth} proposed moving acceptance criteria checks off manual handling.

readings.driver: The less anyone has to check that by hand, the sooner feedback reaches the team.
readings.boundary: She will not accept acceptance criteria staying hands on through the next release cycle.
readings.trade_off: She would accept acceptance criteria staying hands on a while longer if the audit lands first.
readings.fact: That is simply how acceptance criteria checks are run today, by hand.

items.fact: {reliability_ruth} proposed that the hand-off into model evaluation carry a formal sign off.

readings.driver: A formal sign off there would catch a bad evaluation run before it reaches a report.
readings.boundary: She will not accept that hand-off shipping an evaluation without that formal sign off in place.
readings.trade_off: She would accept a lighter check there if the sign off still covers the riskiest runs.
readings.fact: That is simply the sign off status of that hand-off today, nothing formal yet.

items.fact: KPI definitions are still agreed on by hand each cycle.

readings.driver: Automating that agreement would free up time for the data contracts audit instead.
readings.boundary: Nobody will accept KPI definitions staying unreviewed through the next promotion cycle.
readings.trade_off: The team would accept KPI definitions staying hand reviewed if the audit lands first.
readings.fact: That is simply how the KPI definitions get agreed on today.

items.fact: Risk assessment for new data sources is still done by hand.

readings.driver: Automating that review would catch a bad source before it reaches the pipeline.
readings.boundary: Nobody will accept that review being skipped for new data sources.
readings.trade_off: The team would accept that review staying manual a while longer if the audit lands first.
readings.fact: That is simply how new data sources get reviewed today.

items.fact: Data contracts are broken; the consent fields are gone from the schema.

readings.driver: Rebuilding those fields would clear the audit before the next promotion cycle starts.
readings.boundary: Nobody will accept the loyalty feed reopening without those consent fields restored.
readings.trade_off: The team would accept the feed staying closed a while longer if the fields get rebuilt right.
readings.fact: That is simply the state the data contracts schema is in right now.
